# scenario-1 — synthesised cross-source fixture

**NOT anonymised from real user data.** Generated by
`scripts/synthesise_scenario_1_fixtures.php`. Re-run produces
byte-identical output (seeded `mt_srand(20260516)`).

## Empirical contract

- ICS statement period as the PDF prints it: 15 April 2026 → 14 May 2026
- ICS statement period as the app derives it: 2026-04-15 → 2026-05-13, the min
  and max `posted_at` of the 23 charges. A real Mijn ICS statement prints no
  `Periode` line at all — this fixture's is synthetic and nothing parses it —
  so the period is derived, and it is derived from the column membership is
  tested on. The printed end is the last **boekdatum**, one day past the last
  transactiedatum, and a period with one end from each column is the failure
  recorded in [a period derived from one column and tested on
  another](../../../../../.docs/conventions/invariants-from-shipped-failures.md#a-period-derived-from-one-column-and-tested-on-another).
- ICS transaction count: 23 (21 EUR-native + 2 USD FX rows)
- ICS statement total (settled EUR): €847,32 (84732 cents)
- ASN bulk-iDEAL settlement date: 19 May 2026
- ASN own IBAN (synthetic): `NL57ASNB0123456789`
- ASN counterparty IBAN (synthetic): `ICS-CARD`
- PayPal own IBAN: `PAYPAL` (literal, scoped per-user)
- PayPal CSV row count: 14
- PayPal Reference-Txn-ID deterministic chain depth: 3 (parent + Bankstorting + Algemene-valutaomrekening pair)

## Reconciliation variants

| Variant       | Bulk-iDEAL amount (cents) | Delta (cents) | Expected `card_statement.state` | Expected `credit_carry` (cents) | Tolerance used     |
|---------------|---------------------------|---------------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------|
| clean         | 84732                     | 0             | settled                         | 0                                | exact match        |
| overpaid      | 84885                     | +153          | overpaid                        | 153                              | amount_5eur        |
| underpaid     | 84514                     | −218          | partially_settled               | 0                                | amount_5eur        |

The base `asn-camt053.xml` carries the clean amount. The two overlay
JSON manifests (`scenario-1-overpaid.json`, `scenario-1-underpaid.json`)
carry the alternate bulk-iDEAL amount and the expected state-machine
outcomes for the resolver tests to overlay on top of the base XML.

## Locked features

- General Withdrawal NL hand-off: the PayPal CSV row at line 14 carries
  `Bankstorting naar PP-rekening` with the destination IBAN
  `NL57ASNB0123456789` inferable from the parent-row counterparty linkage.
  The PayPal funding resolver creates a deterministic `chain_link` of
  `kind='paypal_funding'` from the parent PayPal `transfer_out` to
  the matching ASN row.
- Deterministic Reference-Txn-ID chain at CSV lines 8–10
  (parent payment + Bankstorting funding sweep): the parent row
  reference appears verbatim in the child's `Reference Txn ID` cell.
- FX-conversion four-row chain at CSV lines 11–14
  (USD parent + EUR Bankstorting + EUR Algemene-valutaomrekening +
  USD Algemene-valutaomrekening) — the shape a real PayPal FX conversion
  produces. Its conversion legs run **opposite** to the ones in
  `Modules/Ingestion/tests/fixtures/paypal/paypal-sample-1.csv`: the euro
  leg here is a credit (`EUR 20,80`) against a `USD -22,50` parent, which
  is PayPal booking each leg by the balance it moved. That is the shape
  that settled an expense as income — see [Invariants written after a
  shipped failure](../../../../../.docs/conventions/invariants-from-shipped-failures.md)
  — so the two fixtures cover both directions and neither should be
  re-signed to match the other.

## Idempotency

Run `php scripts/synthesise_scenario_1_fixtures.php` twice in a row on a
clean filesystem; `git diff --exit-code Modules/Chains/tests/fixtures/scenario-1/`
returns no output.
